articles.title: Steam Frame review: Another best-in-class VR headset by Valve, though virtual realities clash with economic ones
articles.summary: It’s a strange time to be selling a new VR headset, and maybe an even stranger time to be buying one. The supply of original virtual reality games has slowed to a dribble, and just as with Valve’s last hardware launch, the Steam Frame arrives covered in bumps and scrapes from a fight with the worst components shortage in memory. A fight which, judging by how it’ll cost ya £889 / $1,059 at minimum, it lost. However, something else the Frame has in common with the revamped Steam Machine is that as a piece of hardware per se , it’s really quite likeable. Charismatic, even. It’s a happy marriage of core VR capability and genuinely new engineering ideas: some simple practicality boons, some with the potential to change PC games as we know them. And not just the ones you’d play with sweaty goggles on your face. Read more

articles.title: Valve’s Steam Frame VR headset opens for orders, with the cheapest model priced at a lenswatering £889 / $1,059
articles.summary: Valve have just launched the Steam Frame wireless VR headset, finally completing the triumvirate of new hardware – along with the new Steam Machine and Steam Controller – that they unveiled all the way back in November 2025. The review embargo has also lifted, meaning I can tell you that it’s a smart and flexible piece of virtual reality kit . Definitely the most versatile of its kind, in terms of how it lets you play games. Less triumphantly, the Frame has clearly sustained the impact of the same memory shortages and component cost explosions that jacked up the Machine’s pricing and limited its stock. Thus, despite initial plans to make the Frame cheaper than the ultra-premium Valve Index , the Steam Frame starts at £889 / $1,059 / €1,049 for the smaller 256GB model. That rises to £1,089 / $1,299 / €1,279 for the top 1TB version, with several accessory options potentially bumping out the outlay even further. Read more

articles.title: This week in PC games: become a magic girl in Kernel Hearts, a dog commando in Fright Train, or a capital class warship in Sublight
articles.summary: Happy new week all! Over the weekend I banished all thought of rocks, paper or shotguns and volunteered to pick apples at a local orchard. Many wonderful varieties were carefully netted, then jumbled together in a huge mesh bag: speckled golden sours, fit to devour immediately with an appreciative grimace; jolly green cookers, wearing their scabs like medals of honour; sharp little reds that slice up into the clearest white wedges. Such intoxicating fruit! As we blundered around with poles and hard hats, we trampled on dozens of fallen, rotting apples, spicing the air with a sickly pungence. It was then that I saw it: the juiciest apple of all, dangling almost within grabbing distance in a peculiar depth of shade, beneath a tree of somehow abyssal provenance - its leaves salt-rimed and its roots akin to sunken steel anchors. I reached and the apple danced back a metre, becoming luminous. By its light, I perceived the slow parting of enormous crystal fangs. Damn it, Maw! I am trying to pick apples in peace. It's just as well I've brought a second mesh bag of new PC games to feed you. Read more

articles.title: Inside the Omri Hurwitz’s Media Machine That Is Taking Over Tech
articles.summary: For most startups, media is something they try to earn. They hire a PR firm, build a press list, send pitches, and hope a reporter decides the story is worth covering. For Omri Hurwitz Media , the strategy is considerably more ambitious: build a position inside the media ecosystem itself. That distinction helps explain why OHM has become increasingly visible across technology, cybersecurity, venture capital and startup media. The firm says it generates 622% more media coverage than its No. 2 competitor, while its website reports more than 120 coverage placements per client, 50 million-plus monthly impressions and more than 300 clients. The company's advantage is not simply the ability to pitch journalists. It is the network and media infrastructure behind those pitches. From Media Operator To Media Owner OHM was originally built as a PR firm, but founder Omri Hurwitz has increasingly positioned the company as something closer to a media company hybrid. In an interview with Rolling Stone UK , Hurwitz described OHM's evolution from media operator to media owner and investor, with equity interests spanning media publications, television channels, podcasts and social media properties.
